1 tbsp vegetable oil 4 cups chopped leeks (use only white and light green parts of 2 medium leeks) 2 bay leaves 1 tsp dried thyme 1 tsp dried sage (or 1 tbsp fresh) 1/2 tsp salt 2 cups green beans (cut into 1 in. lengths) 3/4 cup vegetable stock 3 cups chopped green cabbage 3 cups cubed butternut squash 3 cups sliced mushrooms Cheese Sauce:
3 tbsp butter 1/4 cup all purpose white flour 1.5 cups warmed vegetable stock 1/2 tsp dijon mustard or similar 1/2 cup grated cheese, parmesan works Salt and pepper to taste Instructions Start with cheddar pastry. Use a food processor and briefly pulse the flour, salt, and butter until the mixture has lumps about the size of peas. Add cheddar and pulse a few times until the mixture resembles a coarse meal. Add the water, a tbsp at a time, pulsing briefly to incorporate. Press the dough into a ball. Wrap in waxed paper or plastic wrap and refrigerate until ready to roll out Make the filling. In a large saucepan or pot, warm oil on medium high and add leeks, bay leaves, thyme, sage and salt. Saute for ~3 minutes. Add green beans and the stock to simmer for 5 minutes. Add cabbage and squash and cook for another 8-10 minutes until the veggies are becoming tender. Add mushrooms and cook for another 3 minutes. Remove from heat and cover. The goal is to have barely tender veggies that will hold their shape in the baked pot pie Make the cheese sauce. In a small saucepan, melt the butter and whisk in the flour, whisking for a couple minutes to “cook” the flour and then continue whisking while slowly adding the vegetable stock and it thickens into a sauce. Add mustard and cheese and whisk until smooth. Stir the sauce into the vegetable filling and season with salt and pepper to taste. Pour this into a 9x13 in. baking dish Preheat the oven to 375°F On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to fit over the baking dish. Cut a few slits in the crust to allow steam to vent for a crisper crust. Place on top of the filling and trim the edges Bake for 40-50 minutes until the crust is golden. Let sit for 10 minutes prior to serving

content: Ingredients 1 cup sugar (white is fine) 1/2 cup all purpose flour 1/2 tsp salt 2 cups milk (whole preferred) 1 tsp vanilla extract 1 tbsp butter 4 large egg yolks Box of vanilla wafers 4-5 ripe bananas 4 egg whites, at room temp 5 tbsp sugar 1/4 tsp cream of tartar 1/2 tsp vanilla extract Instructions Preheat the oven to 375°F and line the bottom of a 9x9 in. baking pan with vanilla wafers Peel and slice the bananas into 0.5 in. rounds. Cover banana slices with plastic wrap to keep from darkening and quickly make pudding Combine sugar, flour and salt in a bowl and stir well. Mash out any lumps In a heavy saucepan, beat egg yolks well. Make medium heat, slowly add flour, milk and vanilla mixture to the egg yolks, stirring constantly. Bring to a gentle boil and when it begins to thicken add the butter, continuing to stir. Keep boiling and stirring until the mixture reaches a nice pudding consistency (be careful to barely have enough heat to boil but not scorch the bottom) Remove from heat Place a layer of banana slices on top of vanilla wafers. Pour half the pudding over it. Put down another layer of vanilla wafers with another following layer of banana slices and cover with remaining pudding Beat the egg whites at high speed (use electric stirrer) until they form soft peaks. Add cream of tartar. At high speed, gradually add the sugar, a tbsp at a time and beat until stiff peaks form. Fold the vanilla into the meringue and spread the meringue over the pudding, sealing it at the sides of the dish Bake for 12-15 minutes until meringue browns

content: Ingredients 2 cups whole milk 3 tbl cornstarch 7/8 cup dark brown sugar 2 large eggs 1/2 tsp salt 1 cup heavy cream 4 tbl unsalted butter 1/8 cup scotch whiskey (or any whiskey works well too) 6 ounces bittersweet chocolate finely chopped Instructions In medium bowl, whisk 1/2 cup of milk with the cornstarch, sugar, eggs and salt. In large saucepan, cook remaining amount of milk with the heavy cream over medium heat until a skin forms on the surface (>a few minutes). Slowly whisk both together in the saucepan, reduce to medium low heat, and whisk fast/constantly until the pudding thickens and just begins to boil (~5 minutes or more). Remove from heat and whisk in the butter and scotch. Spoon the pudding into 6 ounce glasses or jars and refrigerate until set, minimum of 4 hours (preferably overnight). See notes. Meanwhile, to make the scribbles: line a baking sheet with parchment paper (or equivalent). Heat the chocolate in a bowl in the microwave until mostly melted. Stir to mix all together until smooth. Place chocolate in a small Ziploc bag and cut a very small amount from the bottom corner. Squeeze chocolate out onto baking sheet into fun shapes (best to keep each bite 1x2 inches in size, for best dipping). Let set in the fridge for 30 minutes or more. Serve the pudding with 1 or 2 scribbles dipped in the top. One short burst of whip cream on top is nice. Notes Do not short change the pudding mixture set time. This pudding can keep for days so don’t be afraid to make in the morning or the day before. Whisking well is very important. It is super easy for the pudding to come out lumpy if not enough stirring.
summary:
Ingredients

  • 2 cups whole milk
  • 3 tbl cornstarch
  • 7/8 cup dark brown sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 4 tbl unsalted butter
  • 1/8 cup scotch whiskey (or any whiskey works well too)
  • 6 ounces bittersweet chocolate finely chopped

Instructions

  1. In medium bowl, whisk 1/2 cup of milk with the cornstarch, sugar, eggs and salt.
  2. In large saucepan, cook remaining amount of milk with the heavy cream over medium heat until a skin forms on the surface (>a few minutes).
  3. Slowly whisk both together in the saucepan, reduce to medium low heat, and whisk fast/constantly until the pudding thickens and just begins to boil (~5 minutes or more). Remove from heat and whisk in the butter and scotch.
  4. Spoon the pudding into 6 ounce glasses or jars and refrigerate until set, minimum of 4 hours (preferably overnight). See notes.
  5. Meanwhile, to make the scribbles: line a baking sheet with parchment paper (or equivalent). Heat the chocolate in a bowl in the microwave until mostly melted. Stir to mix all together until smooth. Place chocolate in a small Ziploc bag and cut a very small amount from the bottom corner. Squeeze chocolate out onto baking sheet into fun shapes (best to keep each bite 1x2 inches in size, for best dipping). Let set in the fridge for 30 minutes or more.
  6. Serve the pudding with 1 or 2 scribbles dipped in the top. One short burst of whip cream on top is nice.

Notes

  1. Do not short change the pudding mixture set time. This pudding can keep for days so don’t be afraid to make in the morning or the day before.
  2. Whisking well is very important. It is super easy for the pudding to come out lumpy if not enough stirring.

content: Ingredients 3 tablespoons butter, divided 3 large eggs, whisked 2 large carrots, peeled and diced 1 large white onion, diced 1/2 cup frozen peas 4 cloves garlic, minced salt and black pepper to taste 4 cups cooked rice (I prefer short-grain white rice) 5 green onions, thinly sliced (or just one bunch) 4 tablespoons soy sauce, or more to taste 2 teaspoons oyster sauce (optional) 1/2 teaspoons toasted sesame oil (if you have it but not required) Instructions Heat 1/2 tablespoon of butter in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat until melted. Add egg, and cook until scrambled, stirring occasionally. Remove egg, and transfer to a separate plate Add an additional 1 tablespoon butter to the pan and heat until melted. Sauté for about 5 minutes or until the onion and carrots are soft Increase heat to high, add in the remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons of butter, and stir until melted. Immediately add the rice, green onions, soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using), and stir until combined Continue sautéing for an additional 3 minutes to fry the rice, stirring occasionally. (let the rice rest for a bit between stirs so that it can crisp up on the bottom.) This can take longer depending on heat used and make sure to get crispy to preference but not burned Then add in the eggs and stir to combine. Remove from heat, and stir in the sesame oil until combined. Taste and season with extra soy sauce, if needed Serve immediately

Add garlic, ginger and halved chili peppers and saute for another minute Add chicken, salt and saute until chicken is cooked on the outside at least (but doesn’t have to be all the way through yet) Add tomatoes, coriander, cumin, paprika, turmeric, chili pepper and more salt to taste Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes stirring occasionally (make sure heat is not too hot here as it can burn) Add in optional yogurt, black pepper, garam masala and stir well. Top with the chili peppers and optional ingredients and serve Serve over rice or quinoa. Additionally, having fresh naan on the side is great
summary:
Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp butter
  • 3 tbsp oil
  • 1 large onion, finely diced
  • 8 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 inch ginger, minced
  • 2 serrano peppers cut in half
  • 2.5 lb skinless, boneless chicken thighs, diced
  • 8 roma tomatoes
  • 2 tsp coriander
  • 1 tsp cumin
  • 1/2 tsp paprika
  • 1/2 tsp turmeric
  • 1 tsp red chili powder
  • 3 tsp salt
  • Optional: 1/4 cup plain yogurt
  • 2 tsp black pepper or more to taste
  • 1/2 tsp garam masala
  • 3 mild green chili peppers cut in half
  • Optional: 1-2 tbsp julienned ginger
  • Optional: 2 tbsp cilantro

Instructions

  1. In a large wok or sauce pan, heat butter and oil and saute onions until slightly golden. Add garlic, ginger and halved chili peppers and saute for another minute
  2. Add chicken, salt and saute until chicken is cooked on the outside at least (but doesn’t have to be all the way through yet)
  3. Add tomatoes, coriander, cumin, paprika, turmeric, chili pepper and more salt to taste
  4. Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes stirring occasionally (make sure heat is not too hot here as it can burn)
  5. Add in optional yogurt, black pepper, garam masala and stir well. Top with the chili peppers and optional ingredients and serve
  6. Serve over rice or quinoa. Additionally, having fresh naan on the side is great

content: Ingredients 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil 1 medium yellow or white onion, chopped 2 carrots, peeled and chopped 4 garlic cloves, pressed or minced 2 teaspoons ground cumin 1 teaspoon curry powder 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme 1 large can (28 ounces) diced tomatoes, lightly drained 1 cup brown or green lentils, picked over and rinsed 4 cups vegetable broth 2 cups water 1 teaspoon salt, more to taste Pinch of red pepper flakes Freshly ground black pepper, to taste 1 cup chopped fresh collard greens or kale, tough ribs removed 1 to 2 tablespoons lemon juice (1/2 to 1 medium lemon), to taste Instructions Warm the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium heat Once the oil is shimmering, add the chopped onion and carrot and cook, stirring often, until the onion has softened and is turning translucent, about 5 minutes Add the garlic, cumin, curry powder and thyme. Cook until fragrant while stirring constantly, about 30 seconds. Pour in the drained diced tomatoes and cook for a few more minutes, stirring often Pour in the lentils, broth and the water. Add 1 teaspoon salt and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Season generously with freshly ground black pepper. Raise heat and bring the mixture to a boil, then partially cover the pot and reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape Transfer 2 cups of the soup to a blender. Securely fasten the lid, protect your hand from steam with a tea towel placed over the lid, and puree the soup until smooth. Pour the pureed soup back into the pot. (Or, use an immersion blender to blend a portion of the soup.) Add the chopped greens and cook for 5 more minutes, or until the greens have softened to your liking. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in 1 tablespoon of lemon juice. Taste and season with more salt, pepper and/or lemon juice until the flavors really sing. For spicier soup, add another pinch or two of red pepper flakes Serve while hot
summary:
Ingredients

  • 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 medium yellow or white onion, chopped
  • 2 carrots, peeled and chopped
  • 4 garlic cloves, pressed or minced
  • 2 teaspoons ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon curry powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 large can (28 ounces) diced tomatoes, lightly drained
  • 1 cup brown or green lentils, picked over and rinsed
  • 4 cups vegetable broth
  • 2 cups water
  • 1 teaspoon salt, more to taste
  • Pinch of red pepper flakes
  • Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 1 cup chopped fresh collard greens or kale, tough ribs removed
  • 1 to 2 tablespoons lemon juice (1/2 to 1 medium lemon), to taste

Instructions

  1. Warm the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium heat
  2. Once the oil is shimmering, add the chopped onion and carrot and cook, stirring often, until the onion has softened and is turning translucent, about 5 minutes
  3. Add the garlic, cumin, curry powder and thyme. Cook until fragrant while stirring constantly, about 30 seconds. Pour in the drained diced tomatoes and cook for a few more minutes, stirring often
  4. Pour in the lentils, broth and the water. Add 1 teaspoon salt and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Season generously with freshly ground black pepper. Raise heat and bring the mixture to a boil, then partially cover the pot and reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape
  5. Transfer 2 cups of the soup to a blender. Securely fasten the lid, protect your hand from steam with a tea towel placed over the lid, and puree the soup until smooth. Pour the pureed soup back into the pot. (Or, use an immersion blender to blend a portion of the soup.)
  6. Add the chopped greens and cook for 5 more minutes, or until the greens have softened to your liking. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in 1 tablespoon of lemon juice. Taste and season with more salt, pepper and/or lemon juice until the flavors really sing. For spicier soup, add another pinch or two of red pepper flakes
  7. Serve while hot

content: Ingredients 1 lb linguine (cook according to package directions) 6 tbsp olive oil 1 yellow onion, diced small 8 or more cloves garlic, minced 1 cup dry white wine (pinot grigio, chardonnay or sauvignon blanc) 1 tbsp red pepper flakes (more or less to taste) 2 pounds littleneck clams (~40 of them), scrubbed (or 1 lb sea scallops, or 1 lb shrimp) 1 small batch parsley, finely chopped 3 tbsp butter 1.5 tbsp lemon juice (more or less to taste) Instructions Cook pasta to package directions and set aside. (If you cook a smidge less (1 min), less than al dente, that can help the final product soak up more juice) In large saute pan (or pot), over med-high heat, cook the olive oil with onion and garlic until just golden (do NOT burn) Add the wine, red pepper flakes, some salt to taste, clams (or whatever seafood you are using), and all but 2 tbsp of the parsley. Bring to simmer and cook, covered, until clams open (6-8 minutes). Discard any unopened clams Add butter and lemon juice and dissolve into the sauce Add pasta to the saute pan and stir while it cooks for another minute or two (goal is to have pasta soak up the juice). If it becomes too dry add a smidge bit of water Add salt to taste and serve

  4. Add butter and lemon juice and dissolve into the sauce
  5. Add pasta to the saute pan and stir while it cooks for another minute or two (goal is to have pasta soak up the juice). If it becomes too dry add a smidge bit of water
  6. Add salt to taste and serve

content: Ingredients 1 cup all-purpose flour 1/2 tsp baking soda 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 cup unsalted butter, room temperature 1/3 cup granulated sugar 2/3 cup light-brown sugar, packed 2 tsp pure vanilla extract 1 large egg 1 1/2 cups rolled oats 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips Instructions In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour and baking soda; set aside Combine the butter with both sugars; beat on medium speed until light and fluffy Reduce speed to low; add the salt, vanilla, and eggs. Beat until well mixed, about 1 minute Add flour mixture; mix until almost combined Stir in the oats and chocolate chips. Chill dough for one hour to overnight Preheat oven to 375°F Use a small ice cream scooper (two tablespoons) to Drop heaping tablespoon-size balls of dough about 2 inches apart on baking sheets lined with parchment paper Bake until cookies are golden around the edges, but still soft in the center, 8 to 10 minutes Remove from oven, and let cool on baking sheet 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack, and let cool completely Notes Measure your flour correctly! Adding too much flour to the recipe is the most common mistake. The best, and easiest way to measure flour is by using a scale. If you don’t have one then fluff your flour with a spoon, sprinkle it into your measuring cup, and use a knife to level it off Chilling the dough is optional but it created a cookie that spreads out less, concentrates the flavor and dehydrates the dough a bit as well Toasted walnuts make an excellent addition to this cookie. summary:
Ingredients

  • 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 tsp baking soda
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, room temperature
  • 1/3 cup granulated sugar
  • 2/3 cup light-brown sugar, packed
  • 2 tsp pure vanilla extract
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 1/2 cups rolled oats
  • 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips

Instructions

  1. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour and baking soda; set aside
  2. Combine the butter with both sugars; beat on medium speed until light and fluffy
  3. Reduce speed to low; add the salt, vanilla, and eggs. Beat until well mixed, about 1 minute
  4. Add flour mixture; mix until almost combined
  5. Stir in the oats and chocolate chips. Chill dough for one hour to overnight
  6. Preheat oven to 375°F
  7. Use a small ice cream scooper (two tablespoons) to Drop heaping tablespoon-size balls of dough about 2 inches apart on baking sheets lined with parchment paper
  8. Bake until cookies are golden around the edges, but still soft in the center, 8 to 10 minutes
  9. Remove from oven, and let cool on baking sheet 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack, and let cool completely

Notes

  • Measure your flour correctly! Adding too much flour to the recipe is the most common mistake. The best, and easiest way to measure flour is by using a scale. If you don’t have one then fluff your flour with a spoon, sprinkle it into your measuring cup, and use a knife to level it off
  • Chilling the dough is optional but it created a cookie that spreads out less, concentrates the flavor and dehydrates the dough a bit as well
  • Toasted walnuts make an excellent addition to this cookie. Try adding in 1/2 to 1 cup of chopped nuts
  • Your cookies are done when the edges start to brown. The centers will not be raw but they aren’t fully set either

Ingredients Sauce:
6 tbsp butter 1 huge onion (or two med) diced 7-8 cloves of garlic minced Tbsp red pepper flakes Salt to taste 1-2 6-oz can tomato paste (only one is required) two 14-oz can whole peeled tomatoes 2 cups heavy cream 1/2 cup vodka or more to taste 5 oz parmesan cheese (or fancier parmesan if you got it) 1 lb pasta, dealers choice 2 lb meatballs Instructions In a large (3- or 4-quart) saucepan or small Dutch oven, melt butter over medium heat. Add onion, garlic, and red pepper flakes, season lightly with salt, and cook, stirring frequently, until onions are very soft but not browned, about 15 minutes; lower heat if needed to prevent Browning. Meanwhile, in oven or toaster oven, cook the meatballs per package directions. Add tomato paste and cook, stirring, until tomato paste is fragrant and thick, about 3 minutes. Stir in canned tomatoes with their liquid. Bring to a simmer, then cook, stirring often and crushing the whole tomatoes roughly with a spoon, until sauce has thickened slightly, about 10 minutes. Add cream, and stir to incorporate. Transfer sauce to a blender, and blend until very smooth (you may be able to make an immersion blender work, but in our tests the sauce level was too low to safely avoid splattering). Wipe out pot, then return blended sauce to it. Season lightly with salt. In a medium pot of salted boiling water, cook pasta until just shy of al dente, about 3 minutes less than the package directs. About 1 minute before you transfer pasta to sauce, add vodka to tomato sauce and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Add meatballs and simmer a minute. Using a spider skimmer or slotted spoon, transfer pasta directly to sauce pot along with 1/2 cup (120ml) pasta water (alternatively, reserve 2 cups pasta water, then drain pasta in a colander, then add to sauce with 1/2 cup of the reserved water). Increase heat to high, and cook, stirring constantly, until pasta is well coated in sauce and reaches the al dente stage, about 3 minutes. If sauce thickens too much before pasta is ready, add more pasta water in 1/4 cup (60ml) increments as needed. Remove from heat and stir in cheese until thoroughly incorporated into a smooth and creamy sauce. Taste for salt, and season with more if needed. If you can’t detect the vodka at all, you can add a few drops more and stir it in before serving; exactly how boozy you want the sauce is a question of taste, but be careful because a heavy hand will ruin the dish. Spoon pasta and sauce onto warmed serving plates and top with additional grated cheese. Serve immediately.

content: Ingredients 3 pounds gold potatoes 4 hard boiled eggs 1 cup mayonnaise 1/4 cup buttermilk (or just milk in a pinch) 2 tbsp yellow mustard 2 dill pickles diced well Salt and pepper to taste 2 ribs celery sliced relatively small 1/4 cup red onion diced small Instructions Simmer potatoes for 20 minutes. content: Ingredients Broth: 2 tbl vegetable oil 1 large onion, cut in half 1 small hand ginger (few inches at least), roughly sliced 1 bunch cilantro 3 star anise pods 1 cinnamon stick 4 cloves 1 tsp fennel seeds 1 tsp coriander seeds 8 cups of water 6-8 chicken drumsticks (or thighs) 1/4 cup fish sauce 2 tbl rock sugar For serving: 4 servings pho noodles prepared according to package directions 1 small red onion thinly sliced 1/2 cup thinly sliced green onions (white only) 2 cups mixed herbs Cilantro, basil mint 2 cups bean sprouts 1 jalapeño sliced Lime wedges Hoisin sauce and Siracha Instructions Heat oil in pressure cooker (on sauté mode) on high heat until smoking. Add halved onions, ginger, and cook without moving until well charred (~5 minutes). Take this step seriously, more char is good, make it smoke! Lower heat if smoking excessively. Add rest of broth ingredients to pot. Seal pressure cooker and set for high pressure and heat for 30 minutes. Note: time does not include time it takes to get to pressure/temperature. When done, release pressure valve (for electric pressure cookers) and wait until safe to open. Cook noodles according to package directions and set aside. Get ready other serving ingredients and set aside. After opening pressure cooker, remove chicken to cutting board and debone it. Rest of broth should be put through a fine mesh strainer into a clean pot. Discard anything caught in the strainer. To serve: split noodles, chicken, sliced onion, green onion into bowls. Pour broth into bowls. Serve and individuals add herbs, sprouts, peppers, lime, and sauces as desired.

content: Ingredients 1 tbsp butter 3.5 cups finely diced onions (two onions) 2-3 large carrots, finely chopped 12 oz sliced mushrooms (1 package) 1 medium potato, finely diced 1/4 cup all purpose flour 1 cup low sodium vegetable broth 1 cup milk (can be almond or whatever) 1 cup frozen or canned baby green peas 1/4 cup chives (green part of green onions) 1/4 cup parsley 1 tbsp white vinegar 1 large egg yolk 7 oz store bought puff pastry or pie dough, defrosted Instructions Preheat oven to 400°F Melt butter in large sauce pan on medium and add onion, carrots, and potato. Cook until soft (a few minutes). Add mushrooms, salt and pepper. Cook 5 or so minutes until mushrooms are fully shrunk Sprinkle flour over veggies, stir to coat and cook until raw flavor is gone (1-2 minutes). Slowly add broth and milk stirring constantly until smooth. Bring to simmer and cook until slightly thickened Remove from heat and add peas, herbs, and vinegar. Stir to coat. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Put into 8x8 deep baking dish Meanwhile whisk egg together with 2 tsp water and a pinch of salt until mixed Cut dough to fit on top of baking dish (it is OK to fold in edges on corners and sides if slightly oversized). title: Veggie Pot Pie

content: Ingredients 2 tbsp vegetable oil 1 large onion, diced small 3 large carrots, diced small 1 tsp dried thyme 1 cup brown or green lentils 4 tbsp red wine (or less of red wine vinegar) 1.5-2 cups water 1-2 tsp salt 2-3 lbs yukon gold potatoes (buy a 5 pound bag and sort out quantity, see below) Few tsp salt 3 large garlic cloves, peeled but left whole Butter or olive oil (if vegetarian or making vegan) Black pepper 4 cups chopped kale (2 bunches) 2 cloves garlic, chopped roughly Parmesan cheese Instructions (do filling and mashed potatoes concurrently to save time) Filling: In small sauce pan on medium heat, saute onion, carrot and thyme until softened (~5 minutes). Add lentils and wine and stir well, bring to lively simmer. Add 1.5 cups water and bring back to simmer. Lower heat, cover and cook until tender (~40 minutes). Add more water if necessary. Taste at end and add salt if needed. Set aside Mashed potatoes: Get a large/wide soup pot and fill one layer (only one layer) densely with potatoes. Then add water until just the last millimeter of potato is above the water line. Add whole garlic, plenty of salt/pepper and simmer for ~30 minutes or until potatoes are well cooked (more time does not hurt) Remove potatoes and garlic from water (DO NOT discard water or drain) and mash in large mixing bowl. Add butter (or olive oil if making vegan), salt and liquid from pot until you have a good consistency and flavor of mashed potatoes. Add black pepper to taste With final bit of garlic and chopped kale, heat more oil in frying pan and saute garlic briefly before adding kale (as much as you can fit). Add more kale as it shrinks until all is cooked. Stir constantly to avoid burning garlic Combine kale mixture with filling mixture and put in greased baking dish (pick a size so filling is only ~1/2 inch tall in dish and evenly spread). Add mashed potatoes and spread evenly on top with spoon (this layer can be thicker). Sprinkle heavily with parmesan cheese. Cook at 350°F for 25 minutes. During final 2 minutes, set oven to broil and brown the cheesy top (watch carefully so no burning) Remove from oven, slice and serve. It cools quickly enough
summary:
Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp vegetable oil
  • 1 large onion, diced small
  • 3 large carrots, diced small
  • 1 tsp dried thyme
  • 1 cup brown or green lentils
  • 4 tbsp red wine (or less of red wine vinegar)
  • 1.5-2 cups water
  • 1-2 tsp salt
  • 2-3 lbs yukon gold potatoes (buy a 5 pound bag and sort out quantity, see below)
  • Few tsp salt
  • 3 large garlic cloves, peeled but left whole
  • Butter or olive oil (if vegetarian or making vegan)
  • Black pepper
  • 4 cups chopped kale (2 bunches)
  • 2 cloves garlic, chopped roughly
  • Parmesan cheese

Instructions (do filling and mashed potatoes concurrently to save time)

  1. Filling: In small sauce pan on medium heat, saute onion, carrot and thyme until softened (~5 minutes). Add lentils and wine and stir well, bring to lively simmer. Add 1.5 cups water and bring back to simmer. Lower heat, cover and cook until tender (~40 minutes). Add more water if necessary. Taste at end and add salt if needed. Set aside
  2. Mashed potatoes: Get a large/wide soup pot and fill one layer (only one layer) densely with potatoes. Then add water until just the last millimeter of potato is above the water line. Add whole garlic, plenty of salt/pepper and simmer for ~30 minutes or until potatoes are well cooked (more time does not hurt)
  3. Remove potatoes and garlic from water (DO NOT discard water or drain) and mash in large mixing bowl. Add butter (or olive oil if making vegan), salt and liquid from pot until you have a good consistency and flavor of mashed potatoes. Add black pepper to taste
  4. With final bit of garlic and chopped kale, heat more oil in frying pan and saute garlic briefly before adding kale (as much as you can fit). Add more kale as it shrinks until all is cooked. Stir constantly to avoid burning garlic
  5. Combine kale mixture with filling mixture and put in greased baking dish (pick a size so filling is only ~1/2 inch tall in dish and evenly spread). Add mashed potatoes and spread evenly on top with spoon (this layer can be thicker). Sprinkle heavily with parmesan cheese. Cook at 350°F for 25 minutes. During final 2 minutes, set oven to broil and brown the cheesy top (watch carefully so no burning)
  6. Remove from oven, slice and serve. It cools quickly enough
